name: Black Death

religious_factors.summary: Religious interpretations and institutions shaped responses, but religion is not treated as a single causal actor.

description: A major pandemic caused by Yersinia pestis, with mortality estimates varying substantially by source and region.

name: Thirty Years' War

religious_factors.summary: Confessional conflict was an important factor, intertwined with dynastic, territorial and geopolitical interests.

description: A series of interconnected conflicts in Europe involving religious, dynastic, territorial and geopolitical interests.

name: Lisbon Earthquake

religious_factors.summary: Religious interpretations were prominent in contemporary responses, but the disaster was geophysical in origin.

description: A major earthquake and subsequent tsunami and fires devastated Lisbon and surrounding areas.

name: Napoleonic Wars

religious_factors.summary: Religion was not classified as the primary causal factor in this dataset entry.

description: A series of conflicts involving Napoleonic France and shifting European coalitions.

name: Great Famine of Ireland

religious_factors.summary: Religion intersected with Irish social and political divisions, but famine mortality is not assigned to a religion.

description: A prolonged famine caused primarily by potato blight, compounded by social, economic and political conditions.

name: World War I

religious_factors.summary: Religion is not classified as a primary causal factor.

description: A global conflict involving major powers and multiple fronts, with military and civilian losses.

name: 1918 Influenza Pandemic

religious_factors.summary: No religious actor is treated as a causal agent; religious institutions sometimes participated in public responses.

description: A global influenza pandemic occurring during and after World War I.

name: World War II

religious_factors.summary: Religious identity was targeted in some campaigns, notably the Nazi persecution and murder of Jews; religion itself is not treated as the causal actor.

description: A global war involving mass civilian deaths, occupation, systematic persecution and genocide.

sources.title: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum — World War II

name: Great Chinese Famine

religious_factors.summary: Religion is not classified as a causal factor.

description: A catastrophic famine associated with the Great Leap Forward, policy failures, procurement and environmental factors.

name: 1970 Bhola Cyclone

religious_factors.summary: Religion is not classified as a causal factor.

description: One of the deadliest tropical cyclones recorded, striking the densely populated Ganges–Brahmaputra delta.

name: Rwandan Genocide
actors: Extremist Hutu political and militia networks

religious_factors.summary: Religious institutions and individuals were involved in varied ways; religion is not treated as a collective causal actor.

description: A genocide in which extremist networks targeted Tutsi and moderate Hutu populations.

sources.title: United Nations — Outreach Programme on the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda

name: Indian Ocean Earthquake and Tsunami

religious_factors.summary: No religious causal factor; this was a geophysical disaster.

description: A magnitude 9+ undersea earthquake generated a devastating tsunami across the Indian Ocean.
